evidence: src/infrastructure/http.ts: createApp(services: Services) calls only CatalogueService and OrderService methods (listProducts, getProduct, addProduct, placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, transition); no repository access.
src/infrastructure/http.ts: state checks use the domain's isOrderState and ORDER_STATES; transition rules are left to orders.transition; ACTIONS only maps action names to target OrderState values.
src/infrastructure/http.ts: the error-to-HTTP-status mapping is defined only in statusFor and errorHandler.

src/infrastructure/in-memory.ts: InMemoryProductRepository, InMemoryOrderRepository, UuidGenerator and SystemClock implement the domain ports ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator and Clock.

src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root builds the in-memory adapters, injects them into CatalogueService and OrderService, and seeds data through catalogue.addProduct rather than products.save.
Minor: http.ts builds `state must be one of: ${ORDER_STATES.join(", ")}` twice (GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id). Only the message text is repeated; the check itself comes from the domain.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The infrastructure module is one coherent unit that adapts the domain and application layers to the outside world. http.ts is the Express transport adapter and works only through the application services (the Services interface). in-memory.ts provides adapters that implement the domain ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository, IdGenerator, Clock) and contains no business rules. server.ts is the composition root: it wires the adapters into the services and seeds data through CatalogueService.addProduct, not through the repository directly. Domain invariants are not duplicated: order-state membership comes from the domain's isOrderState and ORDER_STATES, and transition legality is left to OrderService.transition (the ACTIONS map only turns an action name into a target state). Error-to-status mapping lives only in statusFor. Two minor issues do not break a rule or invariant: http.ts builds the 'state must be one of' message twice, though the check itself comes from the domain, and in-memory.ts also holds UuidGenerator and SystemClock, which are not in-memory storage.
